I refactored [ActivitySelection.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/034_activity_selection/ActivitySelection.java:1) so the code now has a single canonical result type: [Schedule](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/034_activity_selection/ActivitySelection.java:120).

The new primary API is [optimalSchedule(...)](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/034_activity_selection/ActivitySelection.java:38), with overloads for primitive arrays, `Activity[]`, and `List<Activity>`. The older `activitySelection(...)` and `selectActivities(...)` methods now just project from that result, so the greedy algorithm only exists once. I also pulled the actual greedy pass into [selectFromSortedActivities](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/034_activity_selection/ActivitySelection.java:57), which makes the orchestration path clearer.
